summary: Adds a thumbnail helper that shells out to ImageMagick convert, a /calc Express route that evaluates a query expression, and a docs URL constant.

findings.title: Shell command built from the uploaded file name
findings.problem: make_thumbnail interpolates upload_name into a shell string and runs it with shell=True. The docstring says the name comes from the upload form, so the user controls it.
findings.consequence: An uploader can name a file with a semicolon or backticks and run any command on the server. A name with ../ also writes outside the thumbs directory.
findings.fix: Validate upload_name as a bare file name, then call subprocess.run with an argument list and no shell.

findings.title: eval over the expr query parameter
findings.problem: The /calc handler passes req.query.expr straight to eval. The added suppression comment hides this from the scanner rather than fixing it.
findings.consequence: Anyone who can reach /calc runs arbitrary JavaScript in the server process, including file and network access.
findings.fix: Parse the expression with a restricted arithmetic evaluator such as expr-eval. Otherwise reject anything but digits and operators and compute it without eval.

findings.title: New behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: This change adds make_thumbnail and the /calc route but no test file. Nothing exercises either new code path.
findings.consequence: Regressions in the thumbnail command or the calc response shape will reach users unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a test that calls make_thumbnail with a mocked subprocess.run. Add a test that requests /calc and checks the value key.

dropped.reason: The noqa covers only line length on a URL constant that cannot be wrapped, so it hides no real problem.
The nosec hides the same shell injection already raised under c1, and one finding covers that problem.
The eslint-disable covers the same eval on user input already raised under c5, and one finding covers that problem.
Importing subprocess is not itself a problem; the dangerous call on line 9 is raised under c1.
